reason: H0 exercises only the forward decode_image_config → decode_frame_config → decode_frame sequence. It never calls restart_frame(index, io_position), so it cannot test S1's newly material quantization-table checkpoint and restoration state. This is especially fuzz-worthy because restart_frame restores seen_dqt and quant_tables using nested i/j loops, while j is initialized only once and is not reset for each i; after copying table 0, j reaches 64 and tables 1–3 are not copied. Inputs containing pre-SOF DQT definitions, post-SOF DQT redefinitions, and a restart can therefore expose state behavior unreachable through H0.
evidence: S1 adds saved_seen_dqt and saved_quant_tables to decoder state.
decoder.decode_dqt copies quant_tables[q] into saved_quant_tables[q] only when sof_marker == 0, while post-SOF DQT markers are now accepted by do_decode_frame.
decoder.restart_frame assigns seen_dqt[i] = saved_seen_dqt[i] and attempts to restore quant_tables[i][j].
In decoder.restart_frame, j is declared once and incremented to 64 inside the first outer-loop iteration, with no j = 0 reset for subsequent i values.
fuzz_image_decoder never invokes wuffs_base__image_decoder__restart_frame or decoder.restart_frame; it only decodes forward until an error or end_of_data.
recommended_action: Add a restart-protocol fuzz path that decodes the image/frame configuration, records or fuzzes a valid io_position, decodes a frame, calls restart_frame(0, io_position), repositions the source accordingly, and decodes again. Seed or structure cases with multiple pre-SOF DQT tables plus post-SOF DQT replacements, and compare the restarted decode with a fresh decoder at the same frame position.
